subtheme: Building Better Benchmarks for New Capabilities

subsubthemes.name: Testing what agents can do in realistic environments
subsubthemes.gist: These papers create benchmarks to measure how well AI agents handle real-world tasks like writing code, using command lines, interacting with websites, and navigating game worlds—capturing the complexity of actual tool use.

subsubthemes.name: Measuring reasoning and problem-solving across domains
subsubthemes.gist: These benchmarks evaluate whether models can solve hard reasoning problems—from logic puzzles to financial analysis to scientific research—often requiring multiple reasoning steps and deep domain knowledge.

subsubthemes.name: Checking if models understand specialized fields
subsubthemes.gist: These benchmarks test whether models can handle real problems from specialized areas like medicine, physics, biology, chemistry, and nursing—often using actual data or professional tasks.

subsubthemes.name: Evaluating multimodal and language understanding
subsubthemes.gist: These benchmarks measure how well models work with images, videos, charts, and multiple types of information together—testing understanding beyond just text.

subsubthemes.name: Building benchmarks that evolve and stay challenging
subsubthemes.gist: These papers develop new ways to construct benchmarks dynamically—updating them as models improve, making them harder over time, or generating test cases automatically to prevent overfitting.

subsubthemes.name: Judging quality when answers are subjective
subsubthemes.gist: These benchmarks tackle the hard problem of evaluating outputs that don't have single right answers—like story generation, creative writing, or summarization—often using other models or humans as judges.
